page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 3890 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top 10% of tested servers. Passmark memory testing also ranks in the top tier. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the average tier. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%, while read bandwidth remains average.

This server configuration is suited for workloads requiring high single-threaded CPU speed and substantial local storage, such as static web serving, database operations, and small-scale language model inference. The inclusion of a 3890 GB NVMe SSD provides high storage density relative to the 16 vCPUs, offering qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy applications that do not require multi-threaded compute scaling or GPU acceleration.
